The No. 5 Hoosiers play host to the fourth-ranked Buckeyes with their undefeated record on the line. The winner will have the inside track to the Big Ten Championshiop Game in Indianapolis The reigning national champion, Indiana, hasn't faced a single ranked team, and it's had one of the easier schedules in the Big Ten. The Hoosiers did get a dicey road test against Nebraska last weekend, but that was a nice warm-up for what's to come on Saturday. Despite losing a number of key pieces from last year's team, Indiana still looks like a serious title contender thanks to newcomers Nick Marsh (528 receiving yards and six touchdowns), Turbo Richard (leads Big Ten in rushing yards) and Tobi Osunsanmi (leads the Big Ten in sacks and tackles for loss). Ohio State will be looking for a little revenge after losing to Indiana in the 2025 Big Ten Championship. That loss snapped the Buckeyes' 30-game winning streak over the Hoosiers, so they'll try to start a new one on Saturday. That's entirely possible, largely due to the presence of Heisman Trophy favorite and athletic anomaly Jeremiah Smith , who leads the conference in just about every major receiving category. This is one of the best games on a loaded Week 7 slate, so here is everything you must know as No. 5 Indiana visits No. 4 Ohio State. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Memorial Stadium -- Bloomington, Indiana TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Ohio State vs. Indiana: Need to know Annual top-five matchup: For the first 97 meetings between these teams, there were zero top-five matchups. When the game kicks off Saturday, it will be the third time in as many years that Indiana and Ohio State have played with both teams ranked inside the top five. If we're honest, Indiana was the main reason there were no top-five matchups in the first 97 meetings, but that has changed in a big way now. The Hoosiers have the resources and the coach to compete with the Buckeyes, so we may have a budding Big Ten rivalry on our hands. Smith's historic season: Every week, Smith rewrites the record books at the program, conference and NCAA level. That could continue on Saturday because Smith is just one receiving touchdown shy of matching Michigan legend Braylon Edwards for the most in Big Ten history (39). Smith has already secured the school records for career receptions (211), receiving yards (3,474) and receiving touchdowns (38). He should only add to those totals against a Hoosiers secondary Smith beat for 144 yards last year. Sacking Sayin: One way to make sure Smith never gets the football is to hit Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin while he still has the ball. That's exactly what the Hoosiers did in the Big Ten title game, sacking Sayin five times. Indiana has the personnel to get after Sayin again this time around. Osunsanmi and Stephen Daley have combined for 10 sacks, and Ohio State has allowed 11 sacks of Sayin thus far. The battle between the Indiana defensive front and the Ohio State offensive line in pass protection will be critical. Ohio State vs. Indiana prediction, picks This should be another tremendous game between a pair of national title contenders, and it may very well be a preview of the Big Ten Championship matchup. Having said that, I do wonder how well Indiana's passing defense will hold up for 60 minutes, especially without D'Angelo Ponds in the secondary this time. Ohio State hits enough big plays with Smith to create some breathing room late. Can the Hoosiers take down the Buckeyes ? And Indiana has a whopping 20 sacks in six games. The writing is on the wall – in Sharpie. Expect the Hoosiers to apply a lot of pressure on Sayin. As for the Hoosiers, they have scored at least 20 in every outing in 2026. Then again, Indiana scored six points through three quarters last Saturday at Nebraska. And, on the flip side, Ohio State hasn’t seen a defense half as sturdy as Indiana’s, aside from Texas, which held the Buckeyes to only three points in the second half. If Indiana’s defense strings together four full quarters, it can bottle up this Ohio State offense – or at least keep it at bay (Smith won’t be entirely shut down by any defense this year). And the expectation is that the Hoosiers offense, which has sputtered at times this year, struggles with this Buckeyes defense. It’d be a surprise to see either team score three touchdowns. picks.headline: Ohio State On SI Staff Picks: Can Buckeyes Get Revenge on Indiana in Week 7?
picks.blurb: Ohio State On SI Staff Picks: Can Buckeyes Get Revenge on Indiana in Week 7? Skip to main content SI.COM 2025 Football Bracket Buckeyes In the NFL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES BB This game needs no introduction. Some may argue this is the game Ohio State has been preparing fo r all season long . Now it has a chance to go to Indiana and rewrite a wrong from last December, when it lost the Big Ten Championship game to the Hoosiers, which ultimately led to them completing their undefeated season. Ohio State isn’t undefeated like Indiana is. However, the Buckeyes are rolling through the start of the Big Ten schedule without any real hiccups. Ohio State (5-1, 3-0 Big Ten) has had this game against the Hoosiers (6-0, 3-0 Big Ten) earmarked on the schedule since it was released. So much so that both teams have remained the class of the Big Ten all year long, with a possible elimination scenario in play come December, ahead of the Big Ten title game in Indianapolis. Someone’s supremacy must be disrupted . Will the Buckeyes struggle again, or will the Hoosiers exploit their weaknesses? Check out our staff picks as the game gets underway. Ohio State vs. Indiana Week 7 Outlook Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day watches during the NCAA football game against the Maryland Terrapins at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Oct. 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: noon ET/9 a.m. PT TV Channel: FOX (consult TV Guide or preferred streaming provider for details). Odds: Ohio State -3; over/under is 50.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Location : Memorial Stadium – Bloomington, Ind. Ohio State’s record under Ryan Day : 87-13 (8-6 in postseason bowl games/CFP). Last time vs. Indiana: A 13-10 loss in the Big Ten title game in a top-two showdown. Ohio State leads the series dating back to 1989, 31-1-1. Pregame festivities: Big Noon Kickoff will be there. Ohio State so far this season: 5-1 (3-0 Big Ten) Zain Bando: 6-0 Dylan Buganski : 5-1 Rafael Zamorano : 4-1 (no pick in Week 6 nor Week 7) Chip Minnich : 4-0 (began contributing ahead of Week 3) Zain Bando: Ohio State 28, Indiana 24 There is no such thing as a one-game season, but the Buckeyes may beg to differ. Indiana handed Ohio State one of its two back-to-back losses to end last season and now, on a fall Saturday in Bloomington, the entire year could come down to whether Ohio State can finally sneak up and regain head-to-head dominance and steal a road win. If wideout Jeremiah Smith gets space and gets comfortable thanks to Julian Sayin, and forces the defense to tire Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover, the game could easily deliver a fantastic finish in the closing minutes. We’ll see if the Buckeyes can make it interesting, or better yet, secure a road win that could change the season for good. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 31, Indiana 28 The highly anticipated, top-five Big Ten showdown between the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday hinges on how Ryan Day's squad handles sudden depth issues against an elite Indiana defense. Ohio State faces an uphill battle following a troubling availability report ruling out two of the team's most relied-upon members on offense ~ Austin Siereveld and Ja'Kobi Jackson. With Austin Siereveld missing his second straight game, the loss of the Preseason All-Big Ten selection strips the Buckeyes of their offensive line leader. This forces Gabe VanSickle and right tackle Phillip Daniels into hyper-extended roles against a vicious Hoosier pass rush; Daniels has not played since the loss at Texas on September 12th. Ja'Kobi Jackson, the team's powerhouse short-yardage back and touchdown leader (6 TDs), is sidelined with a surprise ankle injury. While Bo Jackson will shoulder the primary workload, Ja'Kobi Jackson's absence eliminates the physical lightning-and-thunder dynamic Ohio State uses to control the tempo. Could Isaiah West, who missed a key block that led to a pick-six interception in last week's Maryland game, get a chance at redemption? West offers a physical style of play comparable to Ja'Kobi Jackson. The fans who have been clamoring for Legend Bey may see Bey as a larger part of the offensive game plan. Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith will need to be creative in the run game and involve other receiving talents beyond Jeremiah Smith. With a depleted ground game and a reshuffled protection unit, the entire game plan in my estimation rests on the shoulders of junior quarterback Julian Sayin. Sayin has been using his legs to gain positive yardage in recent games and may need to run more frequently than desired by Sayin or the Ohio State coaching staff. The Ohio State defense is going to be tested, as Indiana boasts talented wide receivers in Nick Marsh and Charlie Becker, plus a strong running game led by Turbo Richard. Quarterback Josh Hoover has not yet thrown an interception this season, so perhaps Ohio State defensive coordinator Matt Patricia will be able to scheme some situations that result in a turnover. Expect a classic, physical Big Ten chess match. While Indiana enters the match healthier and with a strong defensive front, Sayin's elite talent and postseason poise will provide just enough explosive plays in a late two-minute drill to secure a tight, field-goal victory for the Buckeyes in Bloomington. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, Indiana 17 There may not be a matchup this team as well as fans circled coming into this season then the rematch of last year’s Big Ten Championship game in what may be Indiana’s biggest home game in program history. There are old and new faces on both sides, and the clash between head coaches Ryan Day and Curt Cignetti may become one of the conference’s greatest rivalries going forward. Ohio State comes into this matchup battle-tested, seeing ranked teams Iowa and Texas on the road and finishing 1-1 in those matchups. This will be Indiana’s first ranked matchup of the season, but they had a comeback victory at Nebraska last week, in which the Cornhuskers should probably have been a ranked team. This matchup will come down to how dominant Indiana can be at the line of scrimmage, as that may be the only position where Indiana may have more talent than the Buckeyes, other than maybe running back. Indiana should be able to run the ball decently and stop the run on the other side. At the end of the day, the secondary for Ohio State should limit the passing game from exploding and another weapon in the passing game has a big game next to Smith, inching Ohio State to a win in this matchup and moving what we may call in 10 years the “Cignetti-Day War” to a 2-1 Buckeye lead. picks.headline: Rece Davis Reveals Ohio State-Indiana Pick for 'Biggest Game' in Bloomington History
picks.blurb: Rece Davis Reveals Ohio State-Indiana Pick for 'Biggest Game' in Bloomington History Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis picked Ohio State to win at Indiana on Saturday, siding with the Buckeyes in a top-five showdown that puts the Hoosiers’ 22-game winning streak on the line in Bloomington. On the College GameDay podcast, Davis joined fellow panelists Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel in taking No. 4 Ohio State (5-1) over No. 5 Indiana (6-0), though he expects a close finish. “I think a field goal at the end decides it one way or the other,” Davis said. Rece Davis explains his Ohio State pick Ohio State head coach Ryan Day takes the team out of the tunnel before the game against the Maryland Terrapins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis called Saturday’s noon ET kickoff on Fox the “ biggest game in the history of Bloomington , Indiana, not played on a basketball court.” It’s a rematch of last December’s Big Ten championship game, which Indiana won 13-10 in Indianapolis on its way to the national title. Davis called Saturday’s noon ET kickoff on Fox the “ biggest game in the history of Bloomington , Indiana, not played on a basketball court.” It’s a rematch of last December’s Big Ten championship game, which Indiana won 13-10 in Indianapolis on its way to the national title. His case against the Hoosiers rests on the streak itself. “When you have a winning streak as long as Indiana’s, longest in the country ... you start having these near misses,” Davis said. “Sooner or later, one gets you, and it can almost reset you a little bit.” Indiana held off Northwestern 29-23 in its Big Ten opener after starting running back Turbo Richard left with an injury, leaning on backup Lee Beebe Jr. for 203 rushing yards. Last Saturday in Lincoln, Indiana trailed Nebraska 17-6 in the fourth quarter before quarterback Josh Hoover hit receiver Nick Marsh for touchdowns of 75 and 44 yards, the second on fourth-and-1. Afterward, Indiana coach Curt Cignetti said his players “ took a deep breath and relaxed and forgot all the garbage in the first half.” Can Ohio State protect Julian Sayin? Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin (10) throws during the college football game against the Maryland Terrapins | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Davis pointed to the Buckeyes’ offensive line as the deciding matchup. “Ohio State has allowed pressure on 27% of its dropbacks this season. That’s 14th in the Big Ten,” Davis said. “That’s not a great formula against Indiana. Indiana does an unbelievable job of getting pressure without blitzing.” Davis pointed to the Buckeyes’ offensive line as the deciding matchup. “Ohio State has allowed pressure on 27% of its dropbacks this season. That’s 14th in the Big Ten,” Davis said. “That’s not a great formula against Indiana. Indiana does an unbelievable job of getting pressure without blitzing.” Indiana leads the Big Ten with 20 sacks, while Ohio State has allowed 11, which ranks 14th in the conference . The Hoosiers also finished last December’s 13-10 win with five sacks and nine tackles for loss. Still, the Buckeyes have done damage when the pocket holds. Quarterback Julian Sayin, who holds No. 1 in our Big Ten quarterback rankings , has thrown for 1,772 yards and 17 touchdowns, and wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has 916 receiving yards and 11 touchdown catches. Ohio State’s offense also ranks second nationally in expected points added per pass, while Indiana’s defense ranks 76th in that measure. And the Buckeyes’ line landed on the Joe Moore Award midseason honor roll on Wednesday. Why Davis still backs Indiana’s offense Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover (10) passes against the Nebraska Cornhuskers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis pushed back on the idea that Indiana’s attack has slipped, comparing Hoover to Fernando Mendoza, who quarterbacked the Hoosiers to last season’s title. Davis pushed back on the idea that Indiana’s attack has slipped, comparing Hoover to Fernando Mendoza, who quarterbacked the Hoosiers to last season’s title. “If Josh Hoover plays 16 games, as Fernando did last year, the numbers are going to be pretty much the same, almost the same,” Davis said. “He’s thrown 17 touchdown passes. I think Fernando finished with 41 last year. You double that to the end of the season, you’re at 34, and then you have the playoff.” Davis also noted that Indiana remains a run-first team. “Turbo Richard leads the conference in runs of 20 yards or longer,” he said. “They average over six yards a carry.” He placed the matchup in rare Big Ten company, too. “Only once have two teams played three consecutive seasons and been in the top five of the AP poll in all three meetings: Michigan and Ohio State in the middle of the legendary Ten-Year War between Bo Schembechler and Woody Hayes,” Davis said. ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took the opposite side this week, picking Indiana as the underdog to extend its streak to 23 games. away.headline: Ohio State vs. Indiana football injury report: Who’s in, who’s out for ranked Big Ten matchup
away.blurb: COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State freshman receiver Brock Boyd will be a game-time decisions for Saturday’s game at Indiana, according to the Big Ten’s final availability report. Boyd was deemed questionable on the first two injury reports of the week. He was downgraded to doubtful Friday. The Buckeyes will be without starting offensive lineman Austin Siereveld, who did not play against Maryland last week and was listed as out throughout this week. Safety Leroy Roker and running back Ja’Kobi Jackson are also out. Linebacker Christian Alliegro, offensive lineman Phillip Daniels, defensive back Jay Timmons and receivers Devin McCuin and Brandon Inniss were not on the injury report, meaning they’re available to play. Ohio State will have a crucial core of players who missed last week’s game back, though. The Buckeyes have been without Daniels, their starting right tackle, since he suffered an injury late in Ohio State’s Sept. 12 loss at Texas. In his absence, Siereveld moved from right guard to right tackle and Gabe VanSickle started at right guard. VanSickle moved to right tackle with Daniels and Siereveld sidelined last week. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said VanSickle will go back to right guard with Daniels reentering the lineup at right tackle. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Ohio State coach Ryan Day provides injury update on Julian QB Sayin
away.blurb: Ohio State is moving forward with the expectation that quarterback Julian Sayin will miss the rest of the season and will be out indefinitely. "We aren't going to put any timeline on his recovery but he's out indefinitely," Ryan Day said on Monday night. " ... based on the nature of the injury, we're putting together a plan for him not being available for the regular season and him not being available for the postseason." “This is all bigger than just one person,” Day continued. “Certainly we don’t want to see (Sayin) get hurt, and we need him. At the same time, we’ll come together and figure this out. We’ve got a good team. When Luke’s in there, we just may need to do things just a little bit differently, but the bye week gives us a chance to regroup on that and put our heads together.” Sayin injured his throwing arm late in the Buckeyes 19-15 win over Indiana on Saturday and missed the last series of the game. True freshman Luke Fahey entered for Ohio State and was 0-of-2 in his one full series. Sayin had thrown for 2,007 yards with 19 touchdowns and four interceptions, two coming against Indiana. He completed 68.2 percent of his passes this season. Ohio State enters the back half of the season at 6-1 and No. 3 in the country following its Indiana win. Fahey, a former three-star recruit, is 9-of-13 passing for 202 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions this season in backup duties. Ohio State has road game against No. 16 USC this weekend, then heads back home to face Oregon and Northwestern, before its final road game of the season against Nebraska . The final game of the season is at home against Michigan . away.headline: No. 3 Ohio State preparing for Julian Sayin to miss rest of regular season, 'doubtful' he will return after arm injury
away.blurb: The coach for No. 3 Ohio State confirmed Tuesday that his star quarterback is going to be out indefinitely after he went down with a right arm injury in their win over Indiana on Saturday. While he doesn't have a specific timeline for Sayin's return, it's "doubtful" that he will be able to play again in the regular season. "We're not going to put any timeline on his recovery, but he is out indefinitely. … Based on the nature of the injury, we are putting together a plan for him not being available for the regular season, and then also him not being available for the postseason," Day said, via the Delaware Gazette's Dillon Davis . "Based on that, if he's not able to return this fall, we'll put together a plan for that as well." Luckily for the Buckeyes, they aren't in a rush to figure out their quarterback situation. They are off this week before a matchup against No. 19 USC in Los Angeles on Halloween, so they have some extra time. Sayin was replaced on Saturday by freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, though he didn't complete either of the two passes he attempted the rest of the way. Indiana had a look to win the game at the end, too, but Nick Marsh's go-ahead touchdown in the final seconds was ruled just out of bounds. Fahey was a three-star Rivals.com recruit out of high school. He has gone 9-of-13 for 203 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions so far this season, though Saturday was the first meaningful time he's spent on the field. The Buckeyes also have Tavien St. Clair, a sophomore who is a former five-star prospect. St. Clair will presumably back up Fahey against USC, should Day stick with Fahey as his starter. Regardless of what plan Day and his staff put together, losing Sayin is a significant blow for the Buckeyes. Replacing him with several big games left on the schedule — including against Oregon, No. 24 Northwestern and Michigan to close out the regular season — and still finding a path to the postseason is not going to be easy. Ryan Day is preparing for a world where Julian Sayin doesn't take the field again at all this season. Sayin was hit hard from his right side as he went to throw the ball in the fourth quarter of the Buckeyes' 19-15 win at Indiana on Saturday. Sayin's throwing arm was pinned awkwardly against his body as he hit the ground, too. Sayin ran off to the locker room, and came back to the sideline in a sling. He didn't play the rest of the way. Sayin went 15-of-29 for 235 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions before he left the game. Sayin has 2,007 passing yards and 19 touchdowns with just four interceptions through seven games this season, his third with the Buckeyes. He was a Heisman finalist last season, too, and finished in fourth in that race. “I think going into the last few games, Luke’s been ahead of Tavien in terms of what we’ve seen,” Day said, via WBNS10 . “But now that we have a bye week, these guys are both going to get a lot of reps … We’re going to play the guy that gives us the best c

away.headline: Ohio State announces injury update on quarterback Julian Sayin
away.blurb: Starting quarterback Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with a forearm injury after taking a massive hit from the pocket. He later returned to the sideline with his arm in a sling. After the game, Ohio State head coach Ryan Day announced that Sayin would be out for “several weeks.” Ohio State held on to win after Indiana wide receiver Nick Marsh stepped out of bounds on what could’ve been a game-winning touchdown pass late in the fourth quarter. Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover had Marsh open, but he was barely out of bounds, giving Ohio State the win. Ohio State notched a massive win over Indiana on Saturday, but it came at a cost. MORE: College football games on today, Week 7 AP Top 25 TV schedule for Saturday Sayin finished the game with 235 yards through the air, two touchdowns, and two interceptions. Freshman quarterback Luke Fahey replaced him and didn’t complete a pass. What happened after Sayin got hurt? The loss snapped Indiana’s 22-game winning streak since the program went undefeated last year and was 6-0 at the start of this season. Who replaces Sayin going forward? The favorite to start is Fahey, a three-star recruit in the 2026 recruiting class, per 247Sports Composite rankings . He was the No. 586 overall recruit in the country before enrolling at Ohio State. Ohio State is 6-1 overall and will play USC in its next game on Halloween after a bye week next weekend. We’ll see if Sayin can make his way back to the lineup before the end of the season.

away.headline: Ohio State’s Julian Sayin out ‘indefinitely ‘ with elbow injury, Ryan Day announces
away.blurb: Ohio State football news: Julian Sayin out 'indefinitely ' with elbow injury NBA Eastern Atlantic Boston Celtics Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day reveals Julian Sayin is out for an unknown amount of time due to an elbow injury. Head coach Ryan Day informed media members on Tuesday that the junior signal-caller is out indefinitely with the injury in his throwing arm, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel. “Ohio State coach Ryan Day said that QB Julian Sayin is out indefinitely,” Thamel reported. “There's a plan being put in place for Sayin not being available for both the regular season and postseason. He said there's no specific timeline on the recovery. He's dealing with an injury on his throwing arm.” “So, first off, we're not gonna put a timeline on [Julian Sayin's] recovery, but he is out indefinitely,” Day said to media members. “And so, what we're trying to do is give Julian and his family the space and privacy to go through this process. “But based on the nature of the injury, we are putting together a plan for him not being available for the regular season and then also him not being available for the postseason,” Day continued. “So, based on that, if he's not able to return next fall, we'll put together a plan for that as well.” Ryan Day said Julian Sayin will out be out indefinitely, and they’re putting a plan together to move forward as if he’s not gonna be available again for Ohio State. home.headline: Ohio State vs. Indiana football injury report: Who’s in, who’s out for ranked Big Ten matchup
home.blurb: COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State freshman receiver Brock Boyd will be a game-time decisions for Saturday’s game at Indiana, according to the Big Ten’s final availability report. Boyd was deemed questionable on the first two injury reports of the week. He was downgraded to doubtful Friday. The Buckeyes will be without starting offensive lineman Austin Siereveld, who did not play against Maryland last week and was listed as out throughout this week. Safety Leroy Roker and running back Ja’Kobi Jackson are also out. Linebacker Christian Alliegro, offensive lineman Phillip Daniels, defensive back Jay Timmons and receivers Devin McCuin and Brandon Inniss were not on the injury report, meaning they’re available to play. Ohio State will have a crucial core of players who missed last week’s game back, though. The Buckeyes have been without Daniels, their starting right tackle, since he suffered an injury late in Ohio State’s Sept. 12 loss at Texas. In his absence, Siereveld moved from right guard to right tackle and Gabe VanSickle started at right guard. VanSickle moved to right tackle with Daniels and Siereveld sidelined last week. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said VanSickle will go back to right guard with Daniels reentering the lineup at right tackle. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. home.headline: Ohio State football releases first injury report vs. Indiana: Who’s in, who’s out for the Buckeyes
home.blurb: Offensive lineman Austin Siereveld, who missed last week’s win against Maryland, was deemed out on Wednesday’s injury report — the first of four reports this week. Running back Ja’Kobi Jackson, who has appeared in every game for the Buckeyes this season, was also listed as out. He has started the last two games for Ohio State, though running back Bo Jackson had more carries in both contests. Receiver Brock Boyd, running back Isaiah West, defensive end Khary Wilder and offensive lineman Deontae Armstrong were listed as questionable. Linebacker Christian Alliegro, defensive back Jay Timmons, offensive tackle Phillip Daniels and receivers Devin McCuin and Brandon Inniss were not on the report, suggesting they’ll be available after missing last week’s win vs. Maryland. While Timmons could return this week, safety Leroy Roker — who has also been sidelined since Sept. 26 — was listed as out. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State plays at Indiana on Saturday in one of the biggest games of the college football regular season. However, the Buckeyes won’t be at full strength for the matchup. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

Our Florida vs. Texas prediction backs the Longhorns to cover the 10.5-point spread, but our college football expert sees even better value in the game total. I'm taking the Texas Longhorns to cover this -10.5 number; it's a small edge, and I wouldn't play it past here. On the other side, the Longhorns' defense ranks 2nd nationally in adjusted EPA per play, 9th against the run and 11th against the pass, while allowing just 29.9% of available yards (5th) . Florida won't trade scores all afternoon. I'll lay it. TOP PICK Florida vs Texas Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 I'm playing the Under 51.5 and would take it down to 50.5 (50%). It's my top pick. Florida already ranks 105th in average 3rd down distance at 7.62 yards , so expect a lot of long-yardage situations and stalled drives. Texas also ranks 6th in defensive EPA per drive, so even when the Gators move the ball, points haven't come easily against this unit. The Texas offense isn't built to push this total either. It ranks 55th in success rate and 67th in EPA per pass, and gains just 46.5% of available yards (70th). Expect the Longhorns to win with long, methodical drives that drain the clock rather than quick-strike scores. Coming off two straight blowouts, the Gators should come out with urgency, and an offense that ranks 8th in EPA per pass can keep them close for a half. Texas's offense isn't built to jump out to fast leads either. The second half is where the Longhorns' advantages show up. Coming off a loss, Texas is eager to get back in the conference title picture with a good showing against the reeling Gators. Here's what you need to know heading into the matchup as The Big Lead locks in our final prediction for this Week 7 college football clash. Texas offensive inconsistency and defensive strength Arch Manning has shown flashes but has been uneven against better competition, with turnovers becoming a recurring issue. Pass protection has been mixed despite solid grades in some metrics, and the run game has lacked consistent explosiveness. Where Texas separates itself is on defense. The unit ranks among the better groups nationally in yards allowed and has been especially effective limiting yards after contact. Rushing off the edges and overall tackling efficiency have been strengths. That could create some real problems for a Florida offense that has looked worn down. Defensive collapse, run game issues at Florida NCAA Football: Mississippi at Florida Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Even during the Gators' win streak, critics sounded the alarm about this defense. The two-game skid has confirmed those worries. Missed tackles and coverage breakdowns have piled up? The total damage? Florida is the SEC's worst defense in total output, explosive plays allowed, and against the pass. It's the second-worst in scoring. On offense, the Florida run game that once looked dominant has been largely shut down by better fronts. Jadan Baugh's production has dropped sharply. After rushing for over 130 yards in four wins, his totals fell to 13 and then 59 yards in two losses. Questions also linger about quarterback availability with Aaron Philo listed as questionable. A potential shift to Tramell Jones Jr. would add even more uncertainty against a Texas defense that flies to the ball. Key matchup dynamics to watch Texas holds clear edges in defensive structure and home-field stability. Florida's ability to create explosive plays through play-action and yards after catch remains a theoretical strength, but recent film shows those opportunities drying up against disciplined units. Scheme-wise, Texas' ability to limit perimeter runs and finish tackles aligns poorly with what Florida has relied on. Manning should face less pressure than he did against Oklahoma, giving him cleaner looks against a secondary that has been vulnerable. Florida vs. Texas prediction: Who wins and why? Texas is the more complete team right now, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Even with offensive questions, the Longhorns' ability to control the line of scrimmage and force Florida into obvious passing situations should decide the game. Florida has the talent to keep stretches competitive, but the recent defensive regression and limited run game make a full road upset unlikely. The Big Lead Prediction: Texas 31, Florida 17

This video created with the assistance of AI. The No. 7 Longhorns (4-1, 1-1 SEC) face stumbling Florida (4-2, 2-2) Saturday morning at Royal-Memorial Stadium. With a second straight loss to the Gators, Texas would be on the verge of losing any hopes of a spot in the College Football Playoff . But a victory would right the ship for the Longhorns, especially if beleaguered quarterback Arch Manning and an error-prone special teams can trim the mistakes and play a clean game. Under first-year coach Jon Sumrall and breakout running back Jadan Baugh , Florida became one of the early-season darlings of college football after knocking off Ole Miss and climbing into the top 10 of the AP rankings. But the Gators have fallen out of the poll following two straight losses, and a porous Florida defense has given up a combined 83 points over the past two weeks to Missouri and South Carolina. Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Florida Gators. No. 7 Texas (4-1, 1-1 SEC) vs. Florida (4-2, 2-2) When: 11 a.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: Finally, football weather. A Friday cold front drops the temperatures near 50 degrees at kickoff and won't rise much above 70. There may be a few clouds but not much chance of rain. Texas vs Florida football betting info Moneyline: Texas -205, Florida +195 Spread: Texas is favored by 10½ points. Over/under : 52½ Texas history: Florida All-time: Texas leads 3-1-1 Last meeting: Florida 29, Texas 21 (Oct. 4, 2025) Most memorable meeting : Texas 7, Florida 7 (1924). A reported crowd of approximately 10,000 fans filled Clark Field, the current location of the Caven Lacrosse and Sports Center across San Jacinto Boulevard from Royal-Memorial Stadium. The Longhorns held on to the tie by stopping heralded Gator fullback Bill Middlekauff four times inside their own 3-yard line in the final minute of the game. MORE: 'Everything we want is is still right in front of us': Texas football eyes glimmer of hope MORE: Gators QB Aaron Philo uncertain to play due to reported injury Know the foe: Florida Last week: Lost to South Carolina, 38-19 Players to watch: RB Jadan Baugh , a 6-foot-1, 225-pound junior, serves as the centerpiece of the Gator offense. He ranks third in the SEC with 672 yards rushing and leads the conference with 12 rushing touchdowns. In two games against Texas over the past two seasons, he racked up 195 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. QB Aaron Philo , a 6-1, 207-pound junior transfer from Georgia Tech, has been solid if not spectacular, but he may miss the Texas game with an injury . He's thrown for 1,341 yards on 70.5% passing with nine touchdowns and three interceptions and has added 104 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Edge Jayden Woods, a 6-3, 245-pound sophomore, may not quite be at the level of Texas All-American edge Colin Simmons, but he's getting closer. The twitchy pass rusher has 4 ½ sacks and six tackles for a loss, and he'll test the Longhorn pass protection. Central Texas connections: Senior TJ Shananan Jr. , a graduate of Westlake High School in Austin, has started all six games at right guard after spending two seasons at Texas A&M and one year at Penn State. Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) runs the ball during the Red River Rivalry game against Oklahoma at the Cotton Bowl on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) When Texas has the ball This seems like a get-right game for Manning, who ranks seventh in the SEC with 224.4 yards a game on 63% passing with 10 touchdowns and five interceptions. Over the past two games against Missouri's Austin Simmons and South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers, Florida's pass defense has allowed a combined 619 yards on 70.8% passing with six touchdown passes and no interceptions. Those two quarterbacks averaged 13.5 yards per completion against the Gators, which could mean lots of action downfield for Texas receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo . Will freshman Derrek Cooper get more snaps at running back for Texas? He showed flashes with a team-high 41 yards rushing against Oklahoma but averages just 3.5 yards per carry for the season. That's even lower than the Longhorns' paltry team average of 3.7 yards a carry. Buoyed by linebacker Myles Graham (41 tackles), the Gators have been respectable against the run while allowing 124.3 yards a game and 3.9 yards a carry. When Florida has the ball Florida won't shy away from the run. It ranks fifth in the SEC with 200.3 yards rushing a game and averages more than 5 yards a carry as a team. Baugh carries the load, but dynamic Duke Clark (265 yards rushing, 7.4 yards per carry) provides an intriguing change of pace. Texas allows just 96 yards rushing a game and 2.8 yards a carry, but linebackers Rasheem Biles (42 tackles) and Justin Cryer (27) are most effective using their speed to chase down backs instead of having to take on linemen. Texas outside corners Bo Mascoe and Kade Phillips have had issues this season, especially when it comes to drawing flags. Florida could test that pair as well as the rest of the secondary if healthy, but that's a big question mark entering Saturday's game. Dallas Wilson (26 catches, 376 yards, three touchdowns) had a breakout game against Texas last season. However, fellow wideout Vernell Brown III has missed the past two games with a knee injury. Brown has 17 receptions for 271 yards and two touchdowns in four games and has also returned two punts for a touchdown. Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles (3) pulls off a broken facemark after an interception during the game against Texas State at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 5, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas vs Florida key matchup Texas center Connor Robertson vs. Florida noseguard Brendan Bett Brendan Bett, a 6-4, 320-pound transfer from Baylor, anchors the interior of the Gators' 3-4 front from his noseguard spot. He's been active with 15 total tackles and three tackles for a loss but doesn't play at the level of the linemen from Oklahoma, Ohio State or Tennessee. If Robertson and guards Dylan Sikorski and Brandon Baker can't clear some running lanes against Bett and the Gators, they may never get the ground game going. Texas vs Florida prediction Thomas Jones: Texas 34, Florida 16. Barring any more special teams disasters or unacceptable turnovers, the Longhorns should have too much firepower for a reeling Florida defense. Danny Davis: Texas. I doubt the offense will have solved all of its problems over the past week, and don't get me started on the special teams. But only minimal improvement from Arch's bunch will be necessary if the Longhorns continue to play well against the run and subdue Jadan Baugh. Cedric Golden: Texas 27, Florida 20. The Horns respond in favorable fashion but questions remain about this offense and its inability to run the ball. Michael Shapiro: Texas 35, Florida 20. Texas coach Steve Sarkisian will get his wish for a fast start with the Longhorns back at Royal-Memorial Stadium, where they enter Saturday eyeing their 24th victory in the last 25 home games. picks.blurb: Florida vs. Texas Final Score Predictions: Experts weigh in on a desperate Gators team heading to Austin - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff 76ers vs. Knicks updates NBA Predictions World Series schedule Week 7 Waiver Wire 49ers are 6-0 Alan Youngblood/Gainesville Sun-Imagn Images, Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Brandon Little, Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 15, 2026 at 6:48 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After suffering back-to-back embarrassing losses, can the Florida Gators get back in the win column against a reeling Texas Longhorns team? The Florida Gators are in a rough spot at 4-2 as they head to Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns on Saturday afternoon. After two blowout losses to the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks on homecoming, Jon Sumrall 's team is in a tough spot. They were at one point being talked about as potentially being the 2019 LSU Tigers from on the precipice of collapsing. It's his first year at the helm, and the talent level still isn't quite there yet. For the Longhorns, they have beaten Ohio State, but are coming off a tough loss in the Red River Rivalry to the Oklahoma Sooners. They are in an interesting spot right now, and a win is a must for both teams. Who will get the win? Our experts made their predictions. Texas 38, Florida 24 Can we trust the Florida Gators? Honestly, no, and that includes the four-game winning streak to start the season with a massive blowout win over Ole Miss. The defense is struggling to generate pressure and the coverage on the back end has been incredibly inconsistent. Even with Texas having lost Red River last week, their success so far this season and offensive talent gets the Longhorns the win. Can the Gators get the win? Absolutely! Will they? I doubt it. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Texas 33, Florida 19 Both teams come in off dismal losses to unranked teams. The Longhorns, who haven't looked dominant this year by any means, gagged away a game they should have won against Oklahoma but for a pick six and a punt block touchdown. Florida got mollywhopped by South Carolina one game after getting throttled by Missouri. As such, it's tough to tell up from down with these two teams. But my mind immediately goes to two things. First, the Horns' front is still nasty, and Florida suddenly can't find any space for Jadan Baugh and the ground game. On the other side, Florida's defense has become a sieve, and I don't trust they've found a way to fix it yet. Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo are too much for the Longhorns, who win comfortably in Austin. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Texas 31, Florida 20 Arch Manning has faced plenty of criticism for his inconsistency this season, but this is the type of matchup that could help him get back on track. Florida's pass defense has been a major weakness, and I expect Manning to take full advantage by delivering his best performance of the 2026 season. The Longhorns have the talent to exploit the Gators' struggling secondary, and Manning should find plenty of opportunities to push the ball downfield and put points on the board. After an uneven stretch offensively, this could be the breakthrough performance Texas needs. Florida should have some success early, particularly with running back Jadan Baugh leading the way. Baugh has been one of the Gators' most productive playmakers, and I expect him to help Florida move the ball and keep the game competitive in the first half. However, Texas has the defensive talent to make adjustments and limit Florida's offensive production as the game progresses. The Gators have struggled to maintain consistency in recent weeks, and that issue will catch up with them again in Austin. Texas pulls away in the second half, with Manning and the offense doing enough to secure a much-needed win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Texas 21, Florida 17 The Gators have fallen off a bit in the last few weeks after starting red hot. Texas is coming off a disappointing loss to Oklahoma. So, you know, Steve Sarkisian is going to be looking to get his team rolling again. Last week probably showed Texas what they should be doing more often on offense. They need to run more quick-game stuff with Arch Manning, because the long, developing routes downfield aren't helping the offense. Their offensive line isn't great, so they need to start running more quick-game plays. I think this past game showed some of that, and Texas still gets the win despite the offense struggling against a decent Florida defense. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Texas 30, Florida 20 As high as I was on the Florida Gators after the Ole Miss win, that hype has come crashing down after games against Missouri and South Carolina. The offense, led by Jadan Baugh, simply hasn't looked the same, and now the availability of starting QB Aaron Philo is in question. As for Texas, the Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing loss of their own after losing Red River to a bad OU team, and they aim to get back on track. Florida's defense has been bad, to say the least, and this game may serve as a great game for Arch Manning nd Texas. Give me the Longhorns here. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Texas 28, Florida 17 Texas and Florida both need wins this week, and the pressure is even higher for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Two losses for Texas at this point in the season would make things very uncomfortable in Austin, and perhaps it would mark the beginning of the end for some important names there. I don't think that's going to happen, though. I think Texas bounces back this week behind a strong defensive performance and looks the part against Florida. If the Longhorns can limit Jaden Baugh, they'll defend home field without much issue. I think Florida hangs around, but the Longhorns put it away in the fourth quarter. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Texas It shouldn't be much of a surprise that none of our experts have picked the Gators, as they have lost our trust after the disastrous performances of the last two weeks. A win here would do wonders to get them back in our good graces. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.headline: Gators Legend Chris Doering Predicts 'Nasty' Gators vs. No. 7 Longhorns Outcome
picks.blurb: Gators Legend Chris Doering Predicts 'Nasty' Gators vs. No. 7 Longhorns Outcome - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff 76ers vs. Knicks updates NBA Predictions World Series schedule Week 7 Waiver Wire 49ers are 6-0 For the Gators to upset Texas, they're going to need a big day from running back Jadan Baugh. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Scott Kennedy Sat, October 17, 2026 at 12:41 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Florida Gators take on the No. 7 Texas Longhorns on Saturday at Noon EST . The Gators will be eager to return to the field after a pair of less-than-stellar performances the last two weeks. Head coach Jon Sumrall admitted earlier this week that he was taking a more hands-on approach to making sure his players understood what it meant to play Florida Gators football. They'll also be giving second-year quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. his first start after seeing mop-up duty the last two weeks. Gators legend Chris Doering appeared on the Paul Finebaum show to preview the Gators at Longhorns, and he was having flashbacks from the last time Florida traveled to Austin. "For whatever reason, I cannot get the idea or the memory of watching Scott Strickland on the sideline two years ago, last time that Florida went to Austin, and I think they were down 42-0 in the first half and 11:00 a.m. (Central) start," Doering said on the show . Doering was off by a touchdown. It was 35-0 en route to a 49-17 Texas win. However, the kickoff time isn't the only similarity Doering points out. Florida started a backup quarterback two years ago as well. "They were without their starting quarterback. Maybe his mobility can help going up against probably the best front seven that they will face the entire season," Doering said of Jones. Sumrall was unhappy with how the Gators played on the lines of scrimmage in their two losses, and Doering is afraid that won't be fixed quickly enough to beat a powerful Longhorns team. "The blueprint's out on beating Florida. It's being able to out-physical them on the line of scrimmage, being able to stop the run. Everything starts with the run game for Florida. Then the secondary is incredibly porous. Something that we were afraid of in the offseason is now coming to light. "Teams are being able to take advantage of it the last couple of weeks, including last week with LaNorris Sellers converted, I think, about five or six 3rd and 10 pluses." Sellers was an incredibly efficient 23 of 35 passing for 279 yards and four touchdowns in the Gamecocks' 38-19 win. They were 10 for 16 overall on third down. Texas managed 382 yards against Oklahoma last week, but they only scored 24 points in the 27-24 loss to the Sooners. Tennessee held them to 262 yards and 20 points in the previous game. Doering thinks this could be the week the Longhorn offense breaks out. "So, I feel like Texas, if you ever wanted a slump buster, this is it for Texas's offense. I think it's going to get nasty, unfortunately, there in Austin. I think Texas wins by multiple touchdowns," Doering finished. The Longhorns present a big challenge to the Gators, but that also means it's a big opportunity to get back into the College Football Playoff conversation with an upset. away.headline: Miami injury report: Is Xavier Lucas playing vs Florida State?
away.blurb: The Miami football team rolled into its off week at a perfect time ahead of today's rivalry showdown with Florida State . A host of key players injured Sept. 18 at Wake Forest and Oct. 3 at Clemson are starting to come back. The final pregame injury report confirmed the return of some important pieces on the defense. The biggest injury issues all year have been on defense as several top cornerbacks, including starters O.J. Frederique and Xavier Lucas, have been out for most of the season. Those problems built up in the Clemson game when leading edge rusher Marquise Lightfoot left in the first half against the Tigers and didn't return. The following players have been ruled out according to the final injury report Saturday: WR Joshua Moore (out for season), RB CharMar Brown (out for season), DB Ja'Boree Antoine, DB O.J. Frederique, OL Max Buchanan, TE Luka Gilbert (out for season). Lucas is set to return to the starting lineup after missing the past four games with an undisclosed injury he suffered in the season opener at Stanford. Heading into Miami's last game Oct. 3 before its bye week, Lucas was listed as questionable until the night before the game, when he was ruled out. If he still can't go today, Bryce Fitzgerald likely remains the starter opposite Ethan O'Connor with additional snaps for Ryan Mack and Camdin Portis, as well. Damari Brown also could start in his place after getting six snaps against Clemson in his own return from injury. Star Malachi Toney, ranked second in the ACC with 604 receiving yards and tied for the lead with six touchdowns, got banged up in both games but never left for long. The No. 3 Hurricanes ' offense will be without starting guard Max Buchanan for a few weeks and he and fellow lineman Matthew McCoy both got hurt against Clemson . Lightfoot ranks second on the team with 19 tackles and leads the way with five sacks and 5.5 tackles for loss. The junior also has a forced fumble. He was the top returning edge rusher from the 2025 team that had one of the most feared defenses in the country backing up Rueben Bain and Akheem Mesidor. The Canes have showcased their depth in the absence of those key players, boasting the No. 1 scoring defense and No. 5 total defense on their way to a 5-0 start. Here's the latest on Miami's injuries, who's expected to play and which absences could impact the game. Will Marquise Lightfoot and Xavier Lucas play? Miami inactives vs Florida State Lightfoot had two tackles and a sack Oct. 3 at Clemson before heading to the locker room in the second quarter. But he was not listed on the injury report for the FSU game, seeming to confirm coach Mario Cristobal's statements from earlier in the week that he will play today. If Lightfoot still can't go, sophomore Herbert Scroggins III likely slides into the starting role opposite Damon Wilson II with Armondo Blount seeing more snaps, as well. The UT defense, who were hung out to dry by the offense, struggled to stop the short yardage offense of Florida. Backup QB Tramell Jones Jr. was able to get the ball out quickly, utilizing a short passing game that got the ball to his wide receivers before the typically stout Texas defensive line could collapse the pocket. Jones was also able to run the ball effectively when called upon. Jones ran for 41 yards on 10 carries. To make matters worse, the best player on this Texas team might be out for an extended amount of time. All-American EDGE Colin Simmons left the game with an apparent knee injury and did not return, eventually being taken to the locker room on a golf cart. Texas defensive lineman Justus Terry and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman, both listed as probable all week, are not on today's report meaning they should be good to go. home.blurb: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium is looking for a bounce-back game out of their Longhorns, a team that was stunned by Oklahoma last week. Now 4-1 (1-1), this is a huge game for Texas to get back on track against a Gators team that hasn't tasted a conference victory since they upset Auburn on the road and then blew out Ole Miss at the Swamp. That said, QB Aaron Philo is still listed as questionable, though at this point everyone knows that it'll be Tramell Jones under center in a hostile environment. Jones has gotten a decent chunk of playing time in games already this year, but this'll be his first start, and it comes with a pair of wide receivers still questionable. Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton both carry the questionable designation heading into the Week 7 matchup. Florida's lone player ruled out against the Longhorns is running back Duke Clark. When looking at Texas's roster, WR Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman have both been ruled out. Unlike Florida, Texas has a pair of players who are listed as probable, not questionable. Defensive lineman Justus Terry and OL Jordan Coleman make up that list. With the quarterback situation in flux due to Kamario Taylor's apparent turf toe injury sustained against Alabama, State enters the week as two touchdown underdogs on the first fall-like Saturday of football season. Coaches on both sides have a fair amount of familiarity with each other having worked together in Oxford from 2020-21 as boss and apprentice. If Lebby finds a way to get Taylor healthy and ready to roll on Saturday, this may be a barn burner inside Tiger Stadium based on the talent at the offensive skill positions for each team. Mississippi State enters the weeked ranked No. 16 nationally, according to the Week 7 AP Top 25 poll. With an extra week to lick its wounds and recover from a double-digit loss to Alabama, there's a possibility the Bulldogs can find a way to pull off a stunner and keep LSU out of the College Football Playoff entirely in Year 1 under Kiffin. The Bulldogs come in at No. 11 in the SEC, and No. 27 in ESPN's Football Power Index poll with a projected overall record of 8-4 following a 4-1 start on the season. picks.blurb: LSU vs. Mississippi State Final Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB After LSU traveled to Lexington last weekend, Lane Kiffin and the Tigers are coming off of a disappointing loss, heading into the Week 7 matchup against Mississippi State . LSU heads into the matchup with a recent loss, while the Bulldogs are also traveling to Baton Rouge after a loss to the Crimson Tide in Week 5. Before the No. 22 LSU Tigers host the No. 16 Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday, the LSU On SI team predicts which team will win and why. Oct 3, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers safety Tamarcus Cooley (0) intercepts a pass from McNeese Cowboys quarterback Jake Strong (not pictured) during the first half at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ross Abboud The time for sloppiness is over, and everyone in LSU’s football program knows it. Ole Miss was a game you could’ve won. Kentucky was a game you should never have lost. That will be LSU’s wake-up call. LSU 48, Mississippi State 24 Brooke Benedict Unlike last weekend's loss to Kentucky, LSU has to get both sides of the ball to play all four quarters, with the defense able to shut down Mississippi State's pass threat, and Sam Leavitt and his receiver options are able to make key plays during possessions. Without any system errors from the offense, defense and special teams, the team will see some much-needed success back at home, being able to win over the Bulldogs and win back their top-ranked reputation. LSU 33, Mississippi State 21 If Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor plays: Kamario Taylor has an incredible ability to control the long ball, which will force LSU's defense to account for that threat almost all of the time, and following the loss to Kentucky, I expect LSU to play a lot more tight man coverage. The LSU offense, clearly more comfortable playing at home, will establish the run with Dilin Jones against the MSST 3-3-5 defense, and LSU will win a close one late in the 4th. LSU 38, Mississippi State 31 If Taylor doesn't play: If Taylor is unavailable in Saturday's game, the MSST backup QB is not a clear answer. Redshirt Freshman Parker Puckett started in place of Taylor against Alabama, but SEC veteran AJ Swann is also a likely option to play. Regardless, I expect the Bulldogs will be less competitive without the SEC TD leader hurling the rock. LSU wins handily at home. LSU 44, Mississippi State 21 Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor (1) waits for the snap during the third quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Adrian Ramirez Adrian Ramirez LSU will bounce back from its overtime loss to Kentucky with a strong performance at home in Tiger Stadium. If both Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell miss or are limited by their injuries, I expect LSU’s defense to be too much for Mississippi State to handle. I think the Tigers come out with a point to prove and get to work proving it. LSU 31, Mississippi State 14 Hannah Garcia While there’s the possibility of Taylor and Bothwell being out for the game, the LSU defense is still missing key pieces in Spears and Whit Weeks. The receivers have struggled to find consistency all season with catching the ball and Sam Leavitt’s interception numbers are also something that I think could cause LSU to lose. Mississippi State 24, LSU 17 LSU is desperate to bounce back after a tough loss against Kentucky. The keys to this game are Kamario Taylor’s health and Mississippi State’s secondary. Taylor is one of college football’s best quarterbacks, and if he’s not healthy, LSU’s defensive game plan changes. Meanwhile, the Bulldogs allow the second-most passing yards per game in the SEC, so I expect Lane Kiffin to open up the playbook and attack that weakness. I think the Tigers handle business at home. LSU 35, Mississippi State 21 Published Oct 16, 2026 BROOKE BENEDICT Brooke Benedict is a sophomore at LSU, majoring in journalism. She is originally from Boulder, Colorado, and enjoys skiing, hiking, and Pilates. She's always enjoyed watching sports and the way sports bring people together. She has spent one semester as a sports columnist for the LSU student newspaper, and is am excited to continue her LSU sports reporting career with On SI. No. 22 LSU welcomes No. 16 Mississippi State to Baton Rouge on Saturday, with the Tigers laying 14.5 points despite the Bulldogs entering as the higher-ranked team. My Mississippi State vs. LSU prediction backs the Tigers' defense to dictate the tempo against a Bulldogs offense dealing with uncertainty at quarterback. Mississippi State standout Kamario Taylor is questionable with a foot injury, and LSU has the defensive personnel to make life difficult regardless of who starts under center. Read on for my analysis and more college football picks for Saturday, Oct. 17. TOP PICK Who will win Mississippi State vs LSU: LSU -14.5 I'll play LSU at -14.5 to 55%. Although Mississippi State has one of the best offenses in the country, ranking fifth in adjusted EPA per play, that production runs through quarterback Kamario Taylor . He's questionable with a foot injury that clearly limited him against Alabama, while leading rusher Fluff Bothwell is also questionable. Even a fully healthy Bulldogs attack would be in for a fight. LSU's defense ranks fourth in adjusted EPA per play and fourth in EPA per pass allowed (-0.26) . Despite a lacklustre performance against Kentucky last weekend, I'm still a believer in this Tigers unit because of those metrics. On the other side, Mississippi State's defense is 101st in success rate allowed and 99th against the pass , giving inconsistent QB Sam Leavitt plenty of room to work, even with his mistakes. LSU ranks third nationally in net adjusted EPA per play, and back home after a painful overtime loss, the Tigers will pull away. Mississippi State vs LSU Over/Under pick: Under 57.5 The Bulldogs' passing game has carried their offense, but they're running into an LSU secondary allowing just a 34.1% passing success rate, the sixth-lowest mark in the country . If Taylor is out or limited, Mississippi State could be relying on a backup against one of the toughest pass defenses it'll face all season. LSU isn't exactly built to light up the scoreboard, either, especially given its QB play this season. Additionally, the Tigers rank 43rd in offensive EPA per play and 63rd in rushing success rate, making long, clock-eating drives more likely than quick scores. With LSU surrendering just a 36% conversion rate on third and fourth downs, points will be harder to come by than this total suggests. Mississippi State vs LSU combo There's a chance LSU's defense controls the game from the opening snap, and this combo attempts to capture that. MSU's offense will need time to settle in, especially with Taylor either limited or out, which gives the Tigers a chance to build an early cushion at home. LSU also owns a +5.4-yard edge in net field position (19th) , setting up short fields that will help the Tigers pull ahead while keeping the total in check. Mississippi State vs LSU prop: Mississippi State team total Under 23.5 Even if Taylor plays, the foot injury that limited him against Alabama makes it hard to expect his usual production, and Mississippi State's path to 24 points is pretty narrow. LSU ranks 10th in defensive EPA per drive and 12th in early-down EPA per play allowed , which puts opponents behind the chains before third down even arrives. If Taylor can't go, Billy Puckett or AJ Swann takes over in a hostile road environment. I don't like their chances. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 15, 2026 at 2:20 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It looked like LSU was about to dominate the college football world when it beat Clemson 51-10 to start the season. But Lane Kiffin's bunch lost to Ole Miss, came back with a few wins, and then last week got outfoxed by Kentucky in a 35-34 overtime loss. And now there's a problem. LSU is talented enough to beat anyone, but it's one more loss away from realistically being out of the College Football Playoff. That won't be easy with a brutal schedule over the second half of the season. Mississippi State has had two weeks to get over the 56-23 loss to Alabama. It isn't an easy slate, but at 4-1, it'll still be in the mix for big things if it can get out of Baton Rouge with a win. Mississippi State vs LSU: Quick Hits LSU starts a run of three home games in the next four weeks, going to Auburn next before hosting Alabama and Texas. Mississippi State starts its own run of four home games in five weeks after this, hosting Oklahoma before going to Texas. LSU has won three straight in the series ever since the 44-34 loss to open up the 2020 season. That came right after the Tigers' national title season. How To Watch Mississippi State vs LSU Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LA – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Mississippi State Will Win The defense will have to step up its game. The Bulldogs have been winning on their amazing offense, but the defense has held its own in key spots. It might be tough to hang with the Tigers blow for blow, so taking the ball away is a must. Mississippi State came up with two takeaways in two of the last three games, and turnovers have been a big issue for LSU, with ten in six games. Why does the defense have to come up big? Why LSU Will Win Mississippi State might be without star quarterback Kamario Taylor. He's trying to get past a leg injury suffered in the Alabama loss, and now he and top running back Fluff Bothwell are questionable at best. There's also the home-field advantage side of this. Ole Miss and Kentucky are good, but LSU should've been better in both road games. At home, the Tigers have been untouchable, winning by a combined score of 194-44 in the four games. Mississippi State vs LSU Prediction, Betting Lines It'll be a different LSU team than the one that walked off the field against Kentucky. It'll be more confident, explosive, and it won't let up – this won't be a back-and-forth fight like it was against the Wildcats. Of course, this changes if Taylor is at 100% for the Bulldogs, but even if he's ready to roll, LSU will be razor-sharp with a much better defensive performance than last week. The No. 19 Bulldogs (4-2, 2-2 SEC) were rolled, 31-0, by No. 21 LSU (5-2, 2-2) at Tiger Stadium on Oct. 17. Taylor's absence was felt, combined with top running back Fluff Bothwell not playing either. Sophomore Billy Puckett , a former walk-on, showed a capability to move MSU down the field in his first career start but was unable to make the same big plays that Taylor does. He threw an ugly interception on the second drive of the game but responded with seven straight completions and a few more impressive plays. It still led to zero points though, the first time MSU's been shut out since 2020 against Alabama, with MSU going 0-for-5 on fourth down. Mississippi State has no open dates remaining with Oklahoma next at Davis Wade Stadium on Oct. 24 (2:30 p.m.). It will also need to get healthier on defense for that game with linebackers Jalen Smith and Zakari Tillman both not playing against LSU and safety Isaac Smith exiting with an injury. Mandatory Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images (Jordan Prather, IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) 1 / 15 LSU football vs Mississippi State time, TV channel, score, updates LSU football vs Mississippi State time, TV channel, score, updates LSU football at Kentucky: Game photos from the sidelines LSU football leads Mississippi State after first quarter Kamario Taylor's health Kiffin called the Bulldogs' sophomore quarterback a "problem" earlier this week. Kiffin's Ole Miss squad saw Taylor in the regular season finale last year and he and current Ole Miss head coach, then defensive coordinator Pete Golding may still be having visions of Taylor gashing the defense. In that game, Taylor ran for 173 yards and two touchdowns. He nearly rushed for more yards than he threw for; he had 178 passing yards. Ole Miss won the game comfortably, 38-19, but as Kiffin said, Taylor has all the tools to be very problematic for defenses. Mississippi State wasn't able to firmly challenge Alabama at home two weeks ago before the off week. Taylor threw a couple of interceptions and fumbled the ball. So, turnovers were a major issues, but the dual-threat quarterback was also limited in what he could as he's been contending with a lower leg injury. It remains to be seen how healthy Taylor will be, but if he's close to 100%, or fully healthy, this game could be very interesting. Sam Leavitt turnover issues getting perfect matchup? All season to this point, LSU junior starting quarterback Sam Leavitt has had turnover problems. He's the only quarterback in college football that has thrown an interception in every game this year and his eight picks lead FBS. It's a very troubling stat and, if that trend continues, more losses are on the way for the Tigers. But is the Mississippi State defense the perfect matchup for Leavitt? Are the Bulldogs just what the doctor ordered for LSU's gunslinger? So far this season, the Bulldogs have two interceptions and their pass defense is among the worst in the SEC. Mississippi State has also only recovered two fumbles. Good news for Leavitt is Mississippi State doesn't force turnovers. Early kickoff makes LSU's matchup with Mississippi State scarier? The earliest LSU has kicked off a game in the first half of the regular season was 6 p.m. CT. And that was last week. Does that make this 11 a.m. kickoff spot scary for the Tigers welcoming in Mississippi State? The Bulldogs have only played one game so far at 11 a.m., the loss to Alabama. But it also had a 2:30 p.m. kickoff at Minnesota, which they won, 38-13. LSU practiced in the mornings during fall camp and in season. So, to Kiffin, there shouldn't been an adjustment for his team. "I think we'll play really well," Kiffin said earlier this week. "We practice in the morning every day. So they're up doing that. It's really more what their clock is. I used to be more concerned when we went to this format of the night games being opposite of their body clock. So I don't see it being an issue." LSU football offensive line play LSU struggled to find traditional balance on offense at Kentucky last week. The Wildcats don't have an awesome rush defense, but were able to keep Tiger running backs Dilin Jones and Harlem Berry from getting much of anything going. They combined for 60 rushing yards. Mississippi State's rush defense has fared better so far this season than Kentucky's has, allowing almost 16 yards on the ground less. The Bulldogs have given up five rushing scores on the season. The play up front from LSU's offense must be better this week for the team to keep the Bulldogs at bay. LSU sports the third best running attack in the SEC at 213 yards per game, but Leavitt has played a large role in that and he leads the team in rushing scores with seven. LSU's offensive line need to open run lanes for Jones and Berry against Mississippi State. LSU vs Mississippi State prediction The last time LSU lost under Kiffin a few weeks ago, it was able to bounce back at home and take care of business. Quarterback Kamario Taylor in head coach Jeff Lebby's high-flying offense poses a legit threat to any defense. And this game being an 11 a.m. kickoff also feels like a prime disaster spot for the Tigers. This game will be high scoring, but the question is: which defense will find enough stops to seal the win? I think LSU gets a couple more stops than Mississippi State's defense that averages giving up almost 40 points a game in SEC play. away.headline: Kamario Taylor injury update: Mississippi State QB downgraded to out vs LSU
away.blurb: Taylor, who was listed on Mississippi State's initial SEC availability report Wednesday as questionable for Saturday's showdown against the 21st-ranked Tigers and downgraded to doubtful on Friday, has been ruled out for the noon ET kickoff in Baton Rouge on Oct. 17. Taylor was listed as questionable on Mississippi State's initial SEC player availability report on Wednesday for Saturday's game vs. LSU. He was later downgraded to doubtful on Friday and has since been ruled out. He was shown in street clothes on ESPN's "College GameDay" on Saturday while wearing a boot. Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify . It's something the Bulldogs will have to do without starting quarterback Kamario Taylor under center. The 6-foot-4 quarterback has been one of the breakout players in the SEC through the first six weeks of the season, as he is tied for the third-most touchdown passes in the country (17) and leads the SEC with 290.0 passing yards per game. The hot start for Taylor took a bit of a halt in Week 5 vs. Alabama, as he completed a season-low 55.9% of his passes for 258 yards and three touchdowns while taking five sacks and throwing for two interceptions. Mississippi State and LSU are set for a noon ET kickoff at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge on Saturday, Oct. 17. Here's the latest on Taylor's injury: Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby offered little clarity on the Bulldogs ' quarterback situation Monday, keeping details brief when asked about the position ahead of this week's game against LSU. "Right now, the focus is getting (Taylor) ready to play and then having the ability to continue to create the depth in the room," Lebby said on Monday. "Billy (Puckett) and AJ (Swann) obviously are the two guys that have been competing since Day 1 in fall camp and really last spring. So, those guys obviously have the ability to get work if (Taylor) wasn't ready to roll." The first-year starting quarterback exited the Bulldogs' Week 5 game vs. Alabama in the fourth quarter with an apparent injury. He was seen on the ESPN broadcast first walking into the locker room with members of Mississippi State's medical staff. As noted by the Clarion Ledger — part of the USA TODAY Network — Taylor was seen wearing a boot on his right ankle for the remainder of the frame once he returned to the sidelines. Lebby noted in his postgame news conference after the 56-23 loss to Alabama that Taylor had been dealing with a prior injury heading into the game. What injury does Kamario Taylor have? Taylor is dealing with an undisclosed lower-body injury. home.headline: Kamario Taylor injury update: Mississippi State QB downgraded to out vs LSU
home.blurb: Taylor, who was listed on Mississippi State's initial SEC availability report Wednesday as questionable for Saturday's showdown against the 21st-ranked Tigers and downgraded to doubtful on Friday, has been ruled out for the noon ET kickoff in Baton Rouge on Oct. 17. Taylor was listed as questionable on Mississippi State's initial SEC player availability report on Wednesday for Saturday's game vs. LSU. He was later downgraded to doubtful on Friday and has since been ruled out. He was shown in street clothes on ESPN's "College GameDay" on Saturday while wearing a boot. Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify . It's something the Bulldogs will have to do without starting quarterback Kamario Taylor under center. The 6-foot-4 quarterback has been one of the breakout players in the SEC through the first six weeks of the season, as he is tied for the third-most touchdown passes in the country (17) and leads the SEC with 290.0 passing yards per game. The hot start for Taylor took a bit of a halt in Week 5 vs. Alabama, as he completed a season-low 55.9% of his passes for 258 yards and three touchdowns while taking five sacks and throwing for two interceptions. Mississippi State and LSU are set for a noon ET kickoff at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge on Saturday, Oct. 17. Here's the latest on Taylor's injury: Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby offered little clarity on the Bulldogs ' quarterback situation Monday, keeping details brief when asked about the position ahead of this week's game against LSU. "Right now, the focus is getting (Taylor) ready to play and then having the ability to continue to create the depth in the room," Lebby said on Monday. "Billy (Puckett) and AJ (Swann) obviously are the two guys that have been competing since Day 1 in fall camp and really last spring. So, those guys obviously have the ability to get work if (Taylor) wasn't ready to roll." The first-year starting quarterback exited the Bulldogs' Week 5 game vs. Alabama in the fourth quarter with an apparent injury. He was seen on the ESPN broadcast first walking into the locker room with members of Mississippi State's medical staff. As noted by the Clarion Ledger — part of the USA TODAY Network — Taylor was seen wearing a boot on his right ankle for the remainder of the frame once he returned to the sidelines. Lebby noted in his postgame news conference after the 56-23 loss to Alabama that Taylor had been dealing with a prior injury heading into the game. What injury does Kamario Taylor have? Taylor is dealing with an undisclosed lower-body injury.
