picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , following us on Twitter/X , and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is it. This is the season for an Oregon team that should be in full rock-and-roll mode at this point, but instead it's been one big, sad trombone of a season. The Ducks are still 3-2 with a not-that-horrible schedule the rest of the way outside of a trip to Ohio State. They lost to UCLA, but they can stay alive in the Big Ten title hunt with one more loss, even if an at-large CFP bid is likely gone with a third defeat and no Big Ten Championship. And they have to do it with Nebraska's former star quarterback, Dylan Raiola – maybe. Nebraska had Indiana cooked, but it turned the stove off too early. The Hoosiers rallied back for a 20-17 win, but that might have been more about the defending national champs not being as good this year than the Huskers being close to fantastic. However, winning in Eugene is still hard, and if Nebraska can do it, it's 6-1 with a favorable schedule – Ohio State comes to Lincoln – and all of a sudden, it's on the fast track to 10-2 – at least – and a possible at-large CFP bid. Nebraska vs Oregon: Quick Hits Oregon ends a good run of home games and goes to Illinois after this. After that, it hosts Northwestern before going to Ohio State. Nebraska starts a run of three road games in four dates, getting a week off before playing Washington, and then it's off to Illinois. The two have never played as Big Ten teams. Oregon won the last meeting 42-35 in 2017. The Huskers are 6-2 overall in the series, with the first win in 1952. How To Watch Nebraska vs Oregon Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 11:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Nebraska Will Win UCLA beat up, battered, and bruised Oregon last week. The Ducks might have knocked out Bruin quarterback Nico Iamaleava with a knee injury, but they were destroyed offensively with seven turnovers and just 272 yards of total offense. Oregon is a mess. Star quarterback Dante Moore is expected to miss another game after suffering a concussion against USC. Dylan Raiola might get his shot against his former team, but he was beyond awful against UCLA. Brock Thomas doesn't have Raiola's talent, but he got the offense moving in the second half. Nebraska gave up two huge touchdowns against Indiana, but held firm the rest of the way. Oregon's offensive problems won't all of a sudden be fixed this week. Oct 10, 2026; Lincoln, Nebraska, USA; Nebraska Cornhuskers quarterback Anthony Colandrea (10) passes against the Indiana Hoosiers during the second quarter at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images Why Oregon Will Win Lost in all of Oregon's misery is a defense that showed up and tried to save the day against UCLA. It's been the only team able to stuff the Bruin running game, and it should do the same against Nebraska, starting by keeping quarterback Anthony Colandrea from doing much on the move. The Huskers can force takeaways – three against Michigan State, two against Maryland – but the Ducks are capable of getting their running game moving a bit to take the pressure off the passing game. And about the quarterback situation, yes, Bob Chesney and the UCLA defense pitched a gem last week. But the week before that, Raiola stepped in and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns in a brilliant fill-in performance for Moore against USC. Nebraska vs Oregon Prediction, Betting Lines This is too fluid to be definitive – Oregon might rotate quarterbacks no matter who starts – but this will be more on the Duck defense. It'll be fantastic against the Nebraska running game, and that will be enough. Oregon is 3-0 when allowing fewer than 140 yards on the ground, and Nebraska managed just 128 against Indiana. This won't be pretty, but it'll be a fascinating late-night battle with a few more points than you might expect. picks.headline: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Oregon
picks.blurb: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Oregon - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff 76ers vs. Knicks updates NBA Predictions World Series schedule Week 7 Waiver Wire 49ers are 6-0 Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Oregon Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Nebraska's loss to Indiana last week stung, with the team dropping a 17-6 lead to the defending national champion. Now the Huskers travel up to Oregon for a 10 p.m. CT matchup, the latest start time for Nebraska since 2014. But other factors in this game make this clash all the more questionable. Dante Moore is out for the game, meaning Dylan Raiola, Brock Thomas or even Akili Smith Jr. will be earning the start. But Raiola is the most poetic option after all and is likely the starter despite a rough outing against UCLA. After going 19-of-25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, Raiola only threw 6-of-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions against the Bruins . He also got strip-sacked in the game. Though it was Raiola's only sack, UCLA still brought the pressure throughout. Raiola's main weakness is pressure, which the Bruins exploited last week. Though Raiola can find ways to stay alive in the pocket and deliver big plays, he rarely takes off downfield and has found himself in rough spots. Thomas took over in the fourth quarter for the Ducks and went 11-of-15 for 156 yards and a touchdown. He did, however, fumble on his opening drive but nearly completed the comeback. But even if Thomas starts, it remains to be seen whether he can replicate that success, especially after seeing Raiola's two-game stretch. Now, Nebraska can get to the quarterback, but the concern comes down to the explosive plays. Indiana pulled off multiple explosive plays last week, despite its struggle to produce points and yardage for most of the game. The Ducks can do the same, especially late in the game. Nebraska ran out of steam in the fourth against Indiana at home early in the afternoon. Now, the Huskers face Oregon on the road after dark. The Ducks almost completed their 17-6 comeback against UCLA, so they can find a way to do the same against Nebraska if needed. The Huskers' defense also needs to be cautious with Oregon's rushing game. Though the Ducks don't strike primarily on the ground, Dierre Hill Jr. and Jordon Davison combined for 216 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 54 carries over the last two games, averaging four yards per carry. Though UCLA did suffocate Oregon's run at times, Nebraska could let a play slip by if it's not careful. Oregon's defense also needs to be cautious, seeing how its last two games panned out. The Ducks held USC to 27 points, but Jayden Maiava still threw for 326 yards and two touchdowns on just 23 completions. Oregon also surrendered 205 passing yards on just 13 completions to UCLA, despite holding it to 17 points. Nebraska could do some damage on the run, however. Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker tallied 109 rushing yards earlier this season against the Ducks. Anthony Colandrea could do the same and help the Huskers score. Jamal Rule, Mekhi Nelson and Isaiah Mozee all could have moments as well after UCLA's Wayne Knight found some holes in Oregon's defensive line. Knight finished with 103 yards on 22 carries. But this game is also make-or-break for Oregon's postseason hopes, especially with Ohio State and even Northwestern coming up. The Ducks also have a talented roster and, despite their issues, can deliver major blows to opponents when momentum is on their side. Nebraska's issues on the line, in the secondary and even a bit on special teams don't help either. All of this, plus the after-dark setting, provides just enough to tip the scales in the Ducks' favor. Unless Nebraska can truly come out and play like a team that can earn a top-25 spot, this matchup will likely be another so-close-but-so-far loss. Game preview, prediction, betting line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff 76ers vs. Knicks updates NBA Predictions World Series schedule Week 7 Waiver Wire 49ers are 6-0 Ryan Clarke Fri, October 16, 2026 at 2:23 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) seek to recapture momentum in what has been a massively disappointing 2026 season so far, and they'll have no time to rest and regroup as confident Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) comes to town. The Cornhuskers are coming off a highly competitive effort in a loss to defending national champions Indiana, while the Ducks have a quarterback battle to work out with Dante Moore still sidelined as he recovers from a concussion. Here is a preview: Oregon (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) vs. Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) When: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 8 p.m. PT Where: Autzen Stadium Latest line: Oregon by 7 Radio: Oregon Sports Network Stream : You can watch this game live with Fubo (free trial), or with DIRECTV (free trial). If you are out of free trials, you can also watch this game with Sling (cheapest streaming plans that include live sports). Streaming broadcasts for this game will be available on these streaming services locally in Oregon and Washington, but may not be available outside of the Pacific Northwest, depending on your location. LOOKING FOR REVENGE? Dylan Raiola will have to earn the opportunity to face his former team in Nebraska. A two-year starter for the Cornhuskers, Raiola has faced external criticism for his decision to transfer to Oregon, but he maintains a strong relationship with Nebraska coach Matt Rhule and several of his former teammates. Raiola's performance against UCLA last week was one of the worst by an Oregon quarterback in recent memory: 6 of 19 passing, 43 yards and two interceptions. This, just two weeks after a highly effective outing in relief of the injured Moore against USC. Raiola was pulled in the fourth quarter against UCLA in favor of Brock Thomas, who almost led a Ducks comeback. Akili Smith Jr. was apparently part of the quarterback competition this week, too. While it is far from a guarantee that Raiola will lead the Oregon offense out onto the field against Nebraska, his personal motivation could be enough to sharpen his focus and help earn him the chance — and perhaps bounce back in a big way performance-wise to lead the Ducks to victory. GETTING A PUSH Whether Raiola or any of the Oregon quarterbacks succeeds depends heavily on the men up front. Oregon's offensive line was dreadful last week after getting a strong push to establish the run just two weeks prior against USC. If the Ducks can't find balance and give Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill a chance to break off big plays, it will be a long day for whoever is tossing the pigskin for the Ducks and staring down Nebraska's edge rushers. Especially with top Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart listed as doubtful as of Thursday evening. Dan Lanning admitted this week that Oregon is still working out who its best five offensive linemen are. For a program that came into the season with major questions at the position and an entire spring and fall camp to figure those things out, that is a very bad sign. A MOBILE THREAT Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea is a talented athlete who can make things happen with his legs. He will provide the biggest test yet for Oregon's front seven in containing a mobile quarterback, one they failed when facing Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker but largely passed against USC's Jayden Maiava. For all the bad that showed up in Oregon's befuddling, 17-15 loss to UCLA last week, the defense played well for the most part. Save for a deep pass on the first play of the game and Wayne Knight's touchdown run in the second quarter, the Ducks looked like the defensive line unit many expected them to be coming into the season. This Saturday, maintaining that level of play will start and end with keeping Colandrea in check. Forcing him into tough situations and not allowing him to improvise into big plays on the ground could be the difference. away.headline: Is Jamir Conn playing against Oregon? Nebraska football injury update
away.blurb: On Friday night, the Huskers released their second-to-last Big Ten Availability report, and Jamir Conn was on it. Conn, a transfer safety who's been one of the team's best defensive backs since arriving in Lincoln, is officially listed as out. He's joined by Rex Guthrie, who is also out and has missed the majority of the 2026 campaign. Senior defensive tackle Riley Van Poppel, who missed Nebraska's game against Indiana, was also listed as doubtful. In the five games he's played this season, Van Poppel has recorded seven tackles and 2.0 sacks. Jamir Conn and Rex Guthrie ruled out as Nebraska football faces Oregon Other Huskers, including Khamir Prescott, Larry Miles, Jase Reynolds, Jacob Bower, and Gabe Moore, have been ruled out since the start of the year. Junior tight end Carter Nelson is the only previously unavailable player no longer listed on the report, so he could see his first game action since Week 3 against North Dakota. Guthrie has battled injuries this season, with his snaps limited to 42, all in nonconference play. But he seemed like a potentially important option, especially with Conn out , given the 574 snaps he logged last year. Guthrie and Conn being out for the game is especially worrisome, as the safety play this season has left much to be desired. Indiana exploited the safety position last week, scoring two fourth-quarter touchdowns over 40 yards, largely because the safeties seemed to misread the plays and didn't provide over-the-top coverage. A 75-yard score, followed by a 44-yard TD pass, both to wide-open receivers, turned a 17-6 Nebraska lead into a 20-17 Indiana win. If there's any good news on the injury front, Oregon has plenty of its own, with quarterback Dante Moore and starting safety Aaron Flowers ruled out earlier this week. Nebraska's safety issues could also be helped by the absence of Oregon's leading receiver Evan Stewart. The wideout was listed as doubtful on both of the last two availability reports . Dante Moore out and Evan Stewart iffy hands Nebraska an Oregon opening it badly needs The Nebraska football team has yet another massive game on its plate in Saturday night's faceoff against Oregon. Unfortunately, the Huskers are not only banged up, but they'll also go into the game without two of their best safeties and one of their best defensive linemen. Conn played just 17 snaps against the Hoosiers but made several key plays before being injured on the first play of the second half. Junior defensive back Caleb Benning replaced the Kansas City-area native for the rest of the game. Benning could be in line for a larger role against the Ducks, though Nebraska defensive coordinator Aurich has emphasized that Nebraska will prioritize getting its best 11 players on the field rather than simply plugging in the next man up. away.headline: Two more injuries leave already ragged Nebraska RB room dangerously thin
away.blurb: Third-string runner Isaiah Mozee was injured against Oregon after running for 28 yards on 4 carries. If that wasn't bad enough, Rhule also said that fullback Vincent Genatone is out for the season. Two more injuries leave already ragged Nebraska RB room dangerously thin Skip to main content Football Nebraska's running game has already had serious problems since it started Big Ten play. Now, not only might the Huskers struggle to find yards, but suddenly the depth in the room is very much in question. On Monday afternoon, head coach Matt Rhule gave a long, wide-ranging press conference that touched on, among other things, NU losing two running backs "for a while" over the past few days. With starting running back Jamal Rule having missed parts or all of three games this season, including most of the matchup against the Ducks, the running back room is suddenly thinner than it has been all season. Nebraska football head coach Matt Rhule confirms multiple running back injuries Rhule did say that the freshman running back is banged up but that he hopes Rule will be able to use the bye week to heal up. There's some indication he could be back in time for the Halloween Night game against Washington. Genatone gave Nebraska 's running back room depth, especially as a goal-line threat with his 225-pound frame. The senior finished his 2026 season with a 13-yard touchdown catch, seven rushing attempts for 10 yards, and two additional scores. Rule got off like gangbusters and led all freshman in college football in rushing yards (329) after three games. However, he was injured in the first quarter of the Michigan State game and missed the entirety of the game againt Maryland. He returned against Indiana but wasn't able to run for anywhere near as many yards as he had been. He was reinjured in the first half against Oregon and didn't play the second half. In total, Rule has just 22 carries for 62 yards in Big Ten play. Mozee has seen most of his action on mop-up duty, but he still got 8 carries for 46 yards and 4 catches for 30 yards in Rule's absence against Maryland. So far this season, he has 44 carries for 223 yards and a touchdown, plus 9 catches for 73 yards. With two weeks to prepare for the Washington Huskies on October 31, Nebraska has time to really get a handle on who will carry the load on Halloween. Mekhi Nelson will almost certainly start at running back and will hopefully be backed up by Rule. If he can't go, Kwinten Ives will likely get his first shot at extended playing time all year. But he seemed like a potentially important option, especially with Conn out , given the 574 snaps he logged last year. Guthrie and Conn being out for the game is especially worrisome, as the safety play this season has left much to be desired. Indiana exploited the safety position last week, scoring two fourth-quarter touchdowns over 40 yards, largely because the safeties seemed to misread the plays and didn't provide over-the-top coverage. A 75-yard score, followed by a 44-yard TD pass, both to wide-open receivers, turned a 17-6 Nebraska lead into a 20-17 Indiana win. If there's any good news on the injury front, Oregon has plenty of its own, with quarterback Dante Moore and starting safety Aaron Flowers ruled out earlier this week. Nebraska's safety issues could also be helped by the absence of Oregon's leading receiver Evan Stewart. The wideout was listed as doubtful on both of the last two availability reports . Dante Moore out and Evan Stewart iffy hands Nebraska an Oregon opening it badly needs The Nebraska football team has yet another massive game on its plate in Saturday night's faceoff against Oregon. Unfortunately, the Huskers are not only banged up, but they'll also go into the game without two of their best safeties and one of their best defensive linemen. Conn played just 17 snaps against the Hoosiers but made several key plays before being injured on the first play of the second half. Junior defensive back Caleb Benning replaced the Kansas City-area native for the rest of the game. Benning could be in line for a larger role against the Ducks, though Nebraska defensive coordinator Aurich has emphasized that Nebraska will prioritize getting its best 11 players on the field rather than simply plugging in the next man up. home.headline: Coach Bret Bielema divulges how injuries reshape Oregon vs. Illinois
home.blurb: Moore missed the last two games, but has participated in practice during those two weeks. Lanning continues to express that the program is handling his return to the active roster with care, but hasn’t yet ruled him out against the Illini. The first injury report is set to be released on Wednesday at 5 p.m. PT. While the Fighting Illini will be without their starter, Bielema faces the challenge of not knowing which opposing quarterback to prepare for. Moore could make his return on the road, or former walk-on Brock Thomas could start for the second consecutive game. Oregon could also let Dylan Raiola pick up where he left off against the Cornhuskers. Raiola has more experience of the two if Moore is unavailable. He has six touchdowns and 515 yards on 64.4 percent completion in 2026, while also having two years of starting experience at Nebraska under his belt, with 2,000-plus passing yards in each of those seasons. Two of the Oregon Ducks’ first five games of the 2026 season came on the road. Following their bye week and two straight games at Autzen Stadium, the Ducks now prepare to fly to the Midwest to take on the Illinois Fighting Illini. Oregon and Illinois played in Eugene in 2024 during the Ducks’ first season in the Big Ten. Oregon won that matchup 38-9, but will play in Champaign for the first time as members of the same conference. Ahead of the Week 8 showdown, Fighting Illini coach Bret Bielema reacted to the challenge of preparing for three different Oregon quarterbacks and acknowledged the quarterback injuries plaguing the Big Ten. Big Ten Quarterback Injuries Impacting Both Teams Bielema opened up by talking about Oregon, showing his respect for coach Dan Lanning and the Ducks’ program. “Obviously, Oregon (played) in a four-quarter game on Saturday,” Bielema said. “I made it til half, and knew I was going to watch that game a lot. But obviously, a lot of respect for Dan and his staff and his program and what they’ve been able to accomplish.” Bielema spoke about the similarities between Illinois and Oregon in the sense that they are both dealing with injuries to their starting quarterbacks. Dante Moore sustained a concussion against the USC Trojans on Sept. 26, ultimately heading to the hospital before returning to Eugene with the team. Meanwhile, Illinois senior quarterback Katin Houser is expected to miss four to six weeks following a procedure to his throwing hand. “I think they’ve kind of experienced the same things in the weekend. Katin (Houser) got hurt,” Bielema said. “There were three or four teams around the league that lost their potential No. 1 guy for a certain part of time. Part of college football that we’re seeing now, and I think the biggest thing for us is take advantage of the moment.” To Bielema’s point, Oregon’s most recent loss to the now-ranked No. 9 UCLA Bruins saw starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava exit with an injury. home.headline: Oregon Ducks football player arrested: What we know so far
home.blurb: Multiple local outlets, including KATU's Hallie DeVore as well as KVAL , reported that Oregon star receiver Evan Stewart was booked at Springfield Municipal Jail on Sunday morning following the comeback victory over Nebraska on Saturday. Stewart, a senior, was ruled out for the game due to injury. Victim Information System in Oregon ( VISOR ) records showed Stewart was booked but out of custody. There is no official comment as of Monday morning from Stewart, Lanning, nor the University of Oregon. His teammate, receiver Dakorien Moore, reportedly posted his bail. Here is more ( via ESPN ): "Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was arrested early Sunday on a charge of driving under the influence of intoxicants. Police in Springfield, Oregon, told local ABC affiliate KATU that Stewart was booked at approximately 7 a.m. PT on Sunday. Stewart was released about an hour later to a third party, fellow Oregon receiver Dakorien Moore, according to KATU." Other reporting indicates that Stewart's driving under the influence of intoxicants had nothing to do with "online rumors" of street racing involving other teammates ( via OregonLive.com ): "Springfield Police told The Oregonian/OregonLive on Sunday that online rumors of street racing involving Oregon football players were unfounded, and that several Oregon players were contacted by police early Sunday morning because they were in the area of a separate pursuit. That pursuit, which resulted in Springfield Police discovering an abandoned vehicle, was unrelated to Stewart's alleged DUII arrest. Springfield PD is no longer pursuing the case involving the abandoned vehicle, an official said." Springfield Police Department told USA TODAY's Ducks Wire that they "had no reason to believe" the car pursuit that evening was connected to the Oregon football team.
